question: AI systems can generate fluent, confident text that is factually wrong, so every fact, score and clinical claim in an AI draft must be verified before it stands in a record.
A report was substantially drafted with AI assistance and signed by the treating therapist. Who is accountable for its content?
options: The practice owner, because they approved the tool
The therapist who signed it, fully and in every respect
Accountability is shared between the therapist and the tool

question: You plan to use an approved recording and transcription tool in a session. What must happen before recording starts?
options: Nothing — approval of the tool covers its use in any session
The participant is told in plain language and their consent is documented
A note is added to the record after the session
The supervisor is copied on the transcript

question: It is acceptable to paste identifiable participant information into an AI tool that has not been approved by the practice owner, provided you delete the conversation afterwards.
An AI tool has drafted a progress note from your session summary. Before it can enter the clinical record, what must happen?
options: Nothing further — approved tools produce record-ready notes
The responsible clinician reviews, corrects and approves every part of it
A colleague spot-checks the first paragraph
It is stored separately until the next supervision session
